back: Charge ÷ size of an ion; Mg²⁺ highest and Ba²⁺ lowest in Group 2.

front: Thermal stability of Group 2 carbonates and nitrates
back: Increases down the group: larger cation, lower charge density, less polarisation of the anion, C–O (N–O) bonds weakened less.
ΔH_sol = −ΔH_latt + ΣΔH_hyd (lattice energy exothermic, from gaseous ions).

front: Why sulfates get less soluble down Group 2
back: Large SO₄²⁻: lattice energy falls a little, cation hydration enthalpy falls a lot → ΔH_sol more endothermic.

front: Why hydroxides get more soluble down Group 2
back: Small OH⁻: lattice energy falls faster than cation hydration enthalpy → ΔH_sol less endothermic.

front: Trend in hydration enthalpy of M²⁺
back: Less exothermic down Group 2 as the ion gets larger (weaker attraction for water molecules).
Distortion of an anion's electron cloud by a nearby cation; greatest for small, highly charged cations and large anions.
It is the CATION that polarises the ANION; the C–O bond in the anion is weakened, not the M–O bond strengthened.
